source: Research for the Grade 2 add/sub word problem pilot, 2026-10-01: standards codes (src/standards, unknownCodes clean), CCSS Table 1 situations (docs/research-k4-problem-types.md), released Grade 3 STAAR, FAST and Smarter Balanced formats, the app survey and the v1 bank audit. Built on Sai's four-axis plan of 2026-09-30. Revised after one review round. Revised 2026-10-02 after Sai's comments and a second review round: row 34 (a two-step equation with the box in the second step), row 35 (a two-step picture), rows 36-42 (state lines past 100: Texas within 1,000, Virginia and Georgia totals to 200, from the official text). On rows 1-33 (numbers and ids unchanged): no-regrouping slips on rows 1-3, GA 2.MDR.5.5 on rows 19 and 24, TX 2.4C on rows 20 and 21, 'none, numbers only' on rows 22 and 23, and objective text naming the state ranges. Revised again 2026-10-02 after Sai's 17:54 UTC comment (no items served by state): decision 3 settled, rows 36-42 on subskill biggerNumberStories, a hint rule on row 33, and no 'serve to' sentences. Then, after Sai's 18:21 UTC comment (keep the state lines, even when only one state prescribes something) and a review round: decisions 4 and 10 settled that rows 32, 33 and 36-42 stay, row 33's number rule fixed and its hint rule kept off the key, hint rules for the state words on rows 20, 21, 30 and 31, and the decision 9 text brought up to Sai's 13:10 UTC answer.
note: Sai approved both Grade 2 add and subtract lists as recommended on 2026-10-02 ("approve both lists as recommended"); per decision 7, VA 2.NS.1g is off row 33. Status is decided in the database. mode_id is wordProblems, the new v2-only topic Sai chose on 2026-10-02 (decision 1 of the review page); models for these rows use wordProblems as modeId, never addition, subtraction or barModels. A reload never overwrites an approved row: moving an approved row to another topic is a deliberate database edit plus re-keying its models and items. While the rows are drafts, a reload carries an edit. Examples are our own wording, with numbers within 100 except the state lines (rows 36-40 to 1,000, row 41 to 1,000, row 42 totals to 200). Rows 32, 33 and 36-42 are state lines with no Common Core code; every kid sees them (no state filter, Sai 2026-10-02 17:54 UTC), and their state codes are tags. Rows 36-42 use subskill biggerNumberStories (decision 4, recommended). Sai, 2026-10-02 18:21 UTC: keep the state lines, even when only one state prescribes something (decision 10 settled). spec.variantMistakes names a variant's own slips where the row's regroup slips can't happen; spec.slips gives each slip's value for the example.

rows.title: Which equation matches a one-step story?
rows.problem_type: Take apart, one part unknown
rows.example: Rosa has 63 red and blue beads. Rosa has 28 red beads. Which equation can be used to find the number of blue beads Rosa has? Choices: 63 − 28 = □, 63 + 28 = □ (added), □ − 28 = 63 (box for the whole), □ − 63 = 28 (box for the whole, numbers swapped). [63 − 28 = □]

The hint names the other word once: 'Some classes call it a number sentence.' Every kid reads 'equation' (no state filter, decision 6).

rules: The take-from step removes the objects from the person: gives them away, loses them, eats them, or uses up something that gets used up (stickers on a card, beads on a bracelet). Never 'uses N to build' with toys that stay, when the question asks 'have now' or 'left'.
The two right equations are the story's equation and the one that solves it.
The hint names the other word once: 'Some classes call it a number sentence.' Every kid reads 'equation' (no state filter, decision 6).

rows.title: Which story matches this equation? (Texas, Florida)
rows.problem_type: Equation to story: take from, change unknown
rows.example: Which story matches 52 − □ = 18? Choices: (A) Pia had 52 marbles. Pia gave some marbles away. Now Pia has 18 marbles. How many marbles did Pia give away? (B) Pia had 52 marbles. Pia gave 18 marbles away. How many marbles does Pia have now? (fits 52 − 18 = □) (C) Pia had 52 marbles. Pia got 18 more marbles. How many marbles does Pia have now? (fits 52 + 18 = □) (D) Pia had some marbles. Pia gave 18 marbles away. Now Pia has 52 marbles. How many marbles did Pia have at first? (fits □ − 18 = 52) [A]

rules: Constraint: the key equals the exact total rounded to the nearest ten, and all four choices differ. With one amount rounding up, one down and the key at most 80, 'both down' is always the key minus 10, 'both up' the key plus 10, and 100 is never the key, so no re-roll is needed.

The hint's steps say to add the two amounts exactly, then ask which ten that total is closest to, and stop there; only the worked solution names the closest ten (the hint-leak check fails a hint that states the key). The exact total is always 1 or 2 below that ten, so any kid can answer without rounding (every kid sees this row, decision 10).

rows.title: Which story matches this three-digit equation? (Texas)
rows.problem_type: Equation to story: take from, change unknown
rows.example: Which story matches 452 − □ = 218? Choices: (A) Ida had 452 arcade tickets. Ida spent some arcade tickets on a prize. Now Ida has 218 arcade tickets. How many arcade tickets did Ida spend? (B) Ida had 452 arcade tickets. Ida spent 218 arcade tickets on a prize. How many arcade tickets does Ida have now? (fits 452 − 218 = □) (C) Ida had 452 arcade tickets. Ida won 218 more arcade tickets. How many arcade tickets does Ida have now? (fits 452 + 218 = □) (D) Ida had some arcade tickets. Ida spent 218 arcade tickets on a prize. Now Ida has 452 arcade tickets. How many arcade tickets did Ida have at first? (fits □ − 218 = 452) [A]
